statement: Let $\triangle ABC$ have $CA = CB$ and $\angle ACB = 120^\circ$; $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. $P$ is a variable point on the circumcircle; $Q \in CP$ with $QP = 2QC$. The line through $P$ perpendicular to $AB$ meets line $MQ$ at a unique point $N$. Prove $N$ lies on a fixed circle.

Let $A = \left\{1 + \dfrac{1}{k} : k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\right\}$. Prove every integer $x \geq 2$ is a product of elements of $A$. For $x \geq 2$, let $f(x)$ be the minimum number of such factors. Prove there are infinitely many pairs $(x,y)$ with $f(xy) < f(x) + f(y)$.

$n$ contestants $C_1, \ldots, C_n$ queue by rules: if $C_i$ has at least $i$ others ahead, she pays 1 euro and moves forward $i$ positions; otherwise the restaurant opens. Prove the process always ends. Find the maximum euros the Jury can collect for each $n$.

Dominoes are placed on an $n \times n$ board ($n \geq 3$) with no overlap. The \textit{value} of a row/column is the number of dominoes covering at least one cell of it. A configuration is \textit{balanced} if all rows and columns have equal value $k$. Prove a balanced configuration exists for every $n \geq 3$ and find the minimum number of dominoes needed.

Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$. Circle $\Omega$ is tangent to segment $AB$ and tangent to $\Gamma$ at a point on the same side of $AB$ as $C$. The angle bisector of $\angle BCA$ meets $\Omega$ at $P$ and $Q$. Prove $\angle ABP = \angle QBC$.

(a) Prove that for every real $0 < t < \frac{1}{2}$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that for every $n$-element set $S$ of positive integers, there exist distinct $x, y \in S$ and $m \geq 0$ with $|x - my| \leq ty$.\n\n(b) Determine whether for every $0 < t < \frac{1}{2}$ there exists an infinite set $S$ of positive integers with $|x - my| > ty$ for all distinct $x, y \in S$ and all $m > 0$.
